summary: DJR's page for Fern, a Venetian oldstyle for screens, staged as a printed book: a centred title page framed by fleurons, then Moby-Dick set in each optical size inside a bordered 'page' column, with red damask chapter bands between sections. The standout is an ornament keyboard plus 9-slice pattern generator that builds border-framed tilings from the Fern Ornaments font; the page ends with the standard DJR cart.

instances.look: A title page on white: 'FERN' in widely tracked titling caps between two mirrored red fleuron clusters, an italic line 'A Venetian oldstyle for screens & other things by David Jonathan Ross' under the name, and a hairline-ruled foot with 'BUY ❖ TRIAL ❖ PDF' in small caps
instances.feel: Quiet, ceremonial, like opening a fine-press book
instances.ux: Buy jumps to #buy; Trial is a form button that adds the Testing license to the cart; PDF downloads the specimen
instances.learn: Build the hero frame from the family's own ornament font (rows of fleuron glyphs typed as text): the decoration is itself a specimen of a family member

instances.feel: Like the first page of a well-set book
instances.learn: Run the intro on as one paragraph with coloured pilcrows: it keeps a solid text colour for judging the face and borrows a pre-modern typographic convention that suits a Venetian revival

instances.look: After a red damask band with a framed 'SPECIMENS' label (02), the opening of Moby-Dick runs through the styles: Text Regular and Text Italic at 24px, then two columns of Micro Regular/Italic at ~16px, a red Text Bold/Regular small-caps paragraph, and two columns of Micro Variable at wght 600 and 500; each sample is captioned in tiny red small caps with its settings, e.g. 'TEXT REGULAR (WGHT 400, OPSZ 12)'
instances.feel: A real book specimen: continuous reading, not word samples
instances.learn: Let one continuous literary text flow through every style and optical size, captioning each with its axis values: the reader experiences the opsz shift (12 at text size, 8 at micro size) while reading

instances.look: Under a red 'ORNAMENTS' band (06): an on-screen keyboard whose keys show each Fern Ornaments glyph in red above its letter (Q–P, A–L, Z–B, lowercase too, plus *, Delete, Return, Space), then a left control column (PATTERN TEXT textarea, Presets 1–12, Grid dimensions X/Y, Canvas symmetry X/Y, Pattern symmetry X/Y, 'Copy plain text') beside a large square tiling of red leaves with a distinct border and corners
instances.feel: A Victorian pattern book turned into a toy
instances.ux: Click keys (or type) to edit a tiny 9-slice template: corners, edges and '*' repeat markers; the generator tiles it to the X×Y grid with optional mirror symmetry; presets load ready-made templates; 'Copy plain text' copies the result to paste as live text
instances.learn: Expose the ornament font through a 9-slice template (corner, edge and fill glyphs plus repeat markers) so a few keystrokes produce a full framed border pattern: it teaches how the ornaments are designed to interlock

reconstruction.behaviour: Template text like 'q*ad*e / ****** / w*Yu*x / x*hJ*w / ****** / z*ad*c' expands to a grid of lines ('qadadadadade', 'wYuYuYuYuYux', 'xhJhJhJhJhJw', … 'zadadadadadc') at 12×12 by default; '*' rows and columns repeat to fill X and Y (number inputs 1–100); symmetry checkboxes mirror the canvas or each tile; output re-renders on every input
